title: TAND - a Point-and-Click Adventure
author: AkahitoDE
selftext:
Hi! This is the trailer for **TAND**, a point-and-click adventure I made for Café Jam 2026 (theme: "One Last Night").

*Tand* is an old German word for trinkets – worthless stuff nobody needs any more. In this game, that's the toys.

One afternoon, a child plays with a new toy built from leftover wooden blocks. "Go on, your turn!" Then someone calls from downstairs, the child has to go, and the lid closes. "I'll be right back."

The box ends up in the attic. Dust, cold, silence. The toys up there have been waiting for decades, some for nearly a hundred years, and they still live by the rules of old children's games. Nobody remembers those rules were ever part of a game. *We sit out. Keep still when it creaks. No laughing, no turning round.* Whoever doesn't play for too long stays down. Whoever plays too loudly brings something on.

The New One doesn't know any of that. He knows one afternoon and one sentence: "Your turn!" And he's sure the child will be back any minute. It did say "right back".

**What's in it**

* Puzzles built from old children's games: dominoes, a die, a counting rhyme, hide-and-seek, Red Light, Green Light
* Fully voiced in English and German – over 2,000 lines per language, around twenty characters
* A 3D world at toy scale
* Prologue, five chapters and an epilogue
* Hints if you get stuck (you can switch them off)
* Windows, mouse only

  
The Game launches on 11.01.2026, and we can't wait to here your feedback \~  
[https://frapstery.itch.io/tand](https://frapstery.itch.io/tand)

comments.author: Wooden_Plant7504
comments.body:
The trailer looks amazing.   
My feedback would be to shorten the trailer in order to add previews of the gameplay. Or intersperse those previews if you don't want to shorten it (although 2 mins is a bit on the longer side).

I have checked your website out but could not see much gameplay there neither.  
Will stay tuned for this as I think this looks cool and original.

As an aside, would you mind sharing what your process is for making this ? How did you make the trailer; the 3d models; what the gameplay is like (I know it is point and click but are you going for 3d point and click or 2.5D, etc); which AI did you use for what (audio, 3d, code), etc ?

replies.author: AkahitoDE
replies.body:
Thanks a lot, really glad you like it!

This is a pure story Teaser-Trailer, but yeah you are right. I will keep that in mind for the Launch Trailer!

To your questions but first some context: TAND started as an experiment. I wanted to find out how much one person can get off the ground in about a month by orchestrating AI tools. So my job was mostly direction & bugfixing: the story, the characters, deciding what goes in, and playing through over and over. The AI tools did most of the building.  
  
Gameplay: It's fully 3D, not 2.5D. You walk through real 3D rooms at toy scale (the main character is 9 cm tall). The camera follows you through the room and switches to set angles during scenes. Apart from that it's classic point-and-click: walk, take, use, combine, talk. Most puzzles come from old children's games, dominoes, a die, a counting rhyme, hide-and-seek, Red Light, Green Light. Holding Shift shows everything you can interact with, and there are optional hints.

Trailer: Everything in it is the actual game running, nothing was rendered separately. Together with Claude I built a small recorder that plays the game's own cutscenes frame by frame at a steady 30 fps, with extra camera moves for some shots. Cutting and mixing are scripted too (ffmpeg). The narrator lines were recorded just for the trailer.

Story, Characters, design and direction: me  
Code: Claude and Codex, with me directing, fixing and testing everything (from code to gameplay).  
3D models: a mix of my own Blender work and props that Codex and Claude built directly in code  
Images: GPT Image 2.5  
Voices and sound effects: ElevenLabs  
Music: Suno and Flow in the game, ElevenLabs Music for the trailer

Thanks for staying tuned!
